In mathematics, an '''eigenform''' (meaning simultaneous Hecke eigenform with modular group SL(2,'''Z''')) is a [[modular form]] that is an [[eigenvector]] for all [[Hecke operator]]s ''T<sub>m</sub>'', ''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2,&nbsp;3,&nbsp;....

Eigenforms fall into the realm of [[number theory]], but can be found in other areas of math and science such as [[analysis]], [[combinatorics]], and [[physics]]. Common examples of eigenforms, and the only non-cuspidal eigenforms, are those of the [[Eisenstein series]]. Another example is the [[Weierstrass's elliptic functions#Modular discriminant|&Delta; function]].

== Normalization ==
There are two different normalizations for an eigenform (or for a modular form in general).

=== Algebraic normalization ===
An eigenform is said to be '''normalized''' when scaled so that the ''q''-coefficient in its [[Fourier series]] is one:

:<math>f = a_0 + q + \sum_{i=2}^\infty a_i q^i</math>

where ''q''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''e''<sup>2''&pi;iz''</sup>. As the function ''f'' is also an eigenvector under each Hecke operator ''T<sub>i</sub>'', it has a corresponding eigenvalue. More specifically ''a''<sub>''i''</sub>, ''i''&nbsp;&ge;&nbsp;1 turns out to be the eigenvalue of ''f'' corresponding to the Hecke operator ''T<sub>i</sub>''. In the case when ''f'' is not a cusp form, the eigenvalues can be given explicitly.<ref>{{cite book | title = Introduction to Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms | url = https://archive.org/details/introductiontoel00kobl_0 | url-access = registration | author = Neal Koblitz | chapter = III.5| year = 1984 | isbn = 9780387960296 }}</ref>

=== Analytic normalization ===
An eigenform which is cuspidal can be normalized with respect to its [[Petersson inner product|inner product]]:
:<math>\langle f, f \rangle = 1\,</math>

== Existence ==
The existence of eigenforms is a nontrivial result, but does come directly from the fact that the [[Hecke operator#Hecke algebras|Hecke algebra]] is commutative.

== Higher levels ==
In the case that the [[modular group]] is not the full SL(2,'''Z'''), there is not a Hecke operator for each ''n''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;'''Z''', and as such the definition of an eigenform is changed accordingly: an eigenform is a modular form which is a simultaneous eigenvector for all Hecke operators that act on the space.
